Allen human RNA: prototype methods

This view uses the Allen Human Brain Atlas normalized microarray dataset. It provides 62 probes for the current 20-gene GEAR-XR library and 3,702 source samples from six adult reference donors, aged 24–57 years. It is not a childhood developmental dataset or a comparison between autistic and non-autistic donors.

What the colors mean

Anatomical-label colors come from the FreeSurfer color lookup table for the existing cortical labels. They identify parcels, not gene expression. These are the original BigBrain/DKT mesh boundaries; the mesh has not been replaced by an Allen human segmentation.

Expression colors show the arithmetic mean of the selected probe’s log2-normalized microarray signals in available samples from the selected donor and matched, same-side source areas. Each available tissue sample has equal weight. Samples are not first averaged by source subdivision. Donors and probes are never pooled. This is a mean of log2 signals, not the logarithm of an arithmetic mean on the original signal scale.

The linear scale spans the minimum and maximum mapped parcel means for that one donor and probe. A changed donor or probe changes the scale. Gray means no matched usable samples; it does not indicate absent expression. A numeric zero is retained as a measurement, never used as a missing-data substitute. Lighting and translucency change apparent surface colors; numeric values are authoritative.

Anatomical matching limits

Forty of the 64 displayed cortical parcels have configured source-name matches, including multiple sampled subdivisions of the same named area. The other 24 have no conservative match and remain unavailable. AHBA anatomical names and DKT parcels are not identical boundaries. Even a same-name match is labeled approximate. No spatial registration, interpolation, voxel map, left-to-right mirroring, nearest-region fallback, or broad-lobe imputation is applied. A donor may have no samples for an otherwise mapped parcel.

Download every parcel’s source-structure IDs, names and rationale. Subcortical samples are preserved in the downloadable data but are not painted onto cortex. Our current human geometry is cortex only, unlike the whole mouse annotation viewer.

Probe identity and quality

Each probe is displayed separately. The initial probe is the lowest numeric probe ID, a deterministic choice that is not a claim of optimal quality. We have not applied the supplemental RNA-seq-based probe reliability metrics, reannotation, or detection filters. A signal value alone does not establish biological detection. Differences across probes or genes must not be interpreted as calibrated abundance differences.

KMT5B is returned by Allen under the legacy symbol SUV420H1; identity is checked against NCBI Gene 51111. The original Allen symbol is retained in the sample-details panel and download. The expression arrays, sample order and metadata are retained from the source responses.

Units and provenance

Allen’s documentation describes log2-normalized signals and per-probe z-scores. We display the normalized expression_level field, not nTPM or protein abundance. Original Allen z-scores are retained in the download but are not used to rank genes. These signals must not be combined with HPA RNA-seq values or mouse ISH energy.

The existing HPA regional-candidate view remains available as a separate evidence dataset. Its genetic-evidence and enrichment rules do not apply to the Allen view.

Original API responses, exact URLs, the FreeSurfer table and SHA-256 checksums are archived in the prototype’s research/human-allen directory. The prepared browser data and anatomical crosswalk are downloadable here. Rebuild using scripts/prepare_human_allen.py; see HUMAN_ALLEN.md in the prototype repository. Allen data remain subject to Allen’s terms; FreeSurfer and BigBrain assets retain their respective licensing.

Transparency

Opacity controls affect rendering only. Smooth material blending provides partial transparency with depth testing. Overlapping surfaces can change apparent colors; use the numeric panel for measurements. No vertex coordinates, boundaries or expression values change. Restore 100% for solid surface colors. Human cortex transparency does not add internal structures that are absent from the mesh.
